land.text: Cyrenaica as Ptolemy Apion left it: 'bequeathed it to the Roman Republic' in 96 BC, organised as a province by 78 BC (infobox 'Roman province (74 BC-643 AD)')

successors.note: The Cyrenaica page's infobox dates the Roman province to 74 BC and its text says 'by 78 BC it was organized as one administrative province together with Crete'; roman-republic books the annexation in 74 (its ledger 154) after a tributary interval from 96. Cliopatria draws the Cyrenaican shape to 92.

capitals.name: Cyrene (Shahhat)
capitals.note: The Pentapolis' chief city and Magas' seat; the page names Cyrene first among the five cities. No page opened says it was a capital in each period.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, 30,697 km2 around the Pentapolis, but held as its own state only in 332-322 (Alexander 'received tribute from the cities'; infobox 'Republic (440-322 BC)') and in revolt 305-300 ('Shortly after Ptolemy declared himself king (c.305 BC), the Cyrenaeans rebelled'); Ptolemaic in 322-305 (Ophellas governor 'from around 322 BC until his death in 308 BC', then 'Ptolemy exercised direct control over Cyrene') and in 300-276 (Magas governor)

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. The shape is the Pentapolis (the page: 'it comprised five cities': Cyrene with Apollonia, Taucheira, Euesperides, Balagrae, Barce), 30.7 K km2 in eastern Libya. The Cyrenaica page: 'in 332 BC' Alexander 'received tribute from the cities after taking Egypt' (Cliopatria starts the shape in 331; the dossier starts in 332). Cliopatria keeps the shape to 292 as independent, but the Ophellas page has Ptolemy I's governor in Cyrene from about 322 to 308 and the Magas page has Ptolemy direct ruler to the revolt of c.305 and Magas governor from c.300, so the independent years are 332-322 (as Macedon's tributary) and 305-300 only. The Carthaginian neighbour in Cliopatria (331-292) is not mentioned on the Magas or Cyrenaica pages; the Arae Philaenorum page puts the frontier at the Altars of the Philaeni near the southern end of the Gulf of Sidra, undated.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, 106,225 km2, but held 276-246: infobox 'King of Cyrenaica: 276-250 BC' (coronation disputed, 283-280 or 276/274); after Magas' death in 250 BC Demetrius the Fair, and on the Cyrenaica infobox a 'Republic (249-246 BC)'; Ptolemaic again from 246 ('Berenice married Ptolemy III in 246 BCE'; infobox 'Nome (246-96 BC)')

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. Cliopatria's Cyrenaica of Magas is 106 K km2, 3.5 times the Pentapolis: the extra 62,000 km2 (246 cells to the east and south) lies in no other Cliopatria shape. The Magas page describes the realm only as Cyrenaica 'located in modern Libya', calls it an 'eparchia' in a treaty of the 260s and has Magas attack 'Egypt from the west' until 'an internal revolt of the nomadic Libyan Marmaridae' stopped him; it gives no border and, on a second reading, says nothing of a hinterland. The hinterland is kept on Cliopatria's word at confidence 1. Cliopatria ends the shape at 248; the dossier keeps it to 246, the year of the reunion with Egypt, because the Magas page (no year) and the Berenice II page ('This marriage led to the re-incorporation of Cyrenaica into the Ptolemaic empire') put the end after Demetrius the Fair. Review fix fx-33 (2026-11-01): explicit years -276 to -247 (the kingdom stands from Magas' coronation in 276 to the eve of the 246 reunion with Egypt, ledger 10); without them the compile drew the shape only from Cliopatria's -272.

correction.text: Cyrene, awarded to Ptolemy VIII: the Cyrenaica cells of the Ptolemaic kingdom's 164 shape (the same cells ptolemaic-kingdom ledger 57 gives up)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix fx-33, 2026-11-01), mirror of ptolemaic-kingdom keyframe _-163, which subtracts the Cyrenaica region from the kingdom for these years. Ptolemy VIII page: "As a result of Roman intervention, Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene" (after his expulsion from Alexandria in 163 BC); he "was persuaded to withdraw from Cyprus, in exchange for continued possession of Cyrenaica" (154), and in 145 "the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene, assume the kingship". The page calls him king in Cyrene but never says it was a separate kingdom; hierarchy.csv draws the land as a constituent of the Ptolemaic kingdom. Shape: the 343 cells of the Cyrenaica region that lie in the Ptolemaic 164 shape (Cliopatria's own Cyrenaica shape has none for these years).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, 116,348 km2, but held 105-75: Apion 'apparently given Cyrene as a separate kingdom ca. 105-101 BC' (Cliopatria 110), 'died in 96 BC without heirs' and 'bequeathed it to the Roman Republic'; Rome's tributary until the province of 74 BC (Cliopatria ends 92)

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so no ratio can be taken. The Cyrenaica page: 'It was separated from the main kingdom by Ptolemy VIII and given to his son Ptolemy Apion' (no dates); its infobox lists 'Kingdom (... 163-96 BC ...)' and, overlapping, 'Nome (246-96 BC)'. The Ptolemy Apion page: 'apparently given Cyrene as a separate kingdom ca. 105-101 BC'; the Ptolemy VIII page: Apion 'King of Cyrenaica from an uncertain date until 96 BC'. Cliopatria starts the shape in 110; the dossier takes 105, the earliest year of the Apion page's span. After 96: 'some confusion exists as to the exact territory Rome inherited' and 'by 78 BC it was organized as one administrative province together with Crete' (infobox 'Roman province (74 BC-643 AD)'). Cliopatria draws the shape to 92; for 91-75 the dossier keeps the same outline as Rome's tributary (roman-republic ledger 125 and 154-155). Review fix fx-33 (2026-11-01): explicit years -105 to -75 (Apion's kingdom from ca. 105, ledger 11; Rome's tributary from 96 to the province in 74, ledger 12-14); without them the compile started the shape at Cliopatria's -110, five years before the kingdom and while the land was still Ptolemaic.

region.text: the Pentapolis: Cyrene, Apollonia, Taucheira, Euesperides, Balagrae and Barce

ledger.note: 332: The five Greek cities of the Cyrenaican Pentapolis, a republic since 440 on the page's infobox, submit to Alexander the Great. Page silent on a founding: the cities were already there; the map life begins with Alexander's year (Cyrenaica page: 'in 332 BC', Cliopatria's shape starts in 331).

region.text: the Pentapolis, paying tribute: 'Alexander the Great in 332 BC, who received tribute from the cities after taking Egypt'

ledger.note: 332: The Pentapolis becomes a tributary of Alexander. 'The Persians were followed by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, who received tribute from the cities after taking Egypt.' Recorded from the vassal's side: the cities are macedonian-empire's tributary, so macedonian-empire's gain of Cyrenaica at 332 (its ledger 26) should be the matching vassal_start; the year is the page's, the status is my reading of 'received tribute'.

region.text: the Pentapolis, no longer Macedon's tributary

ledger.note: 322: The Pentapolis ceases to be Macedon's tributary when Ptolemy's army takes it. The Cyrenaica infobox ends the 'Republic' at 322 BC; macedonian-empire's own ledger (43, 49) gives 'Egypt and Libya' to Ptolemy in 323/321.

region.text: the Pentapolis, taken by Ptolemy I's army and governed by Ophellas: 'sent, in 322 BC, at the head of a considerable army'

ledger.note: 322: Ptolemy I's general Ophellas takes Cyrenaica. The Ophellas page: sent 'in 322 BC, at the head of a considerable army' to exploit a civil war in Cyrenaica, then 'Ophellas remained as its governor', 'from around 322 BC until his death in 308 BC'; the Cyrenaica infobox: 'Republic (440-322 BC)', 'Nome (322-276 BC)'. The Berenice II page dates the incorporation 'in 323 BCE, by Ptolemy I Soter' and the Cyrenaica page says only 'formally annexed by Ptolemy I Soter' (undated); 322 is the year of the army. After Ophellas died in November 308 the Magas page has 'Ptolemy exercised direct control over Cyrene'.
305: Cyrene rebels against Ptolemy I. 'Shortly after Ptolemy declared himself king (c.305 BC), the Cyrenaeans rebelled.' The land returns to the cities' own hands until the reconquest.
About 305: the revolt of Cyrene against Ptolemy opens; Ptolemy's reaction is on the page only as the reconquest 'around 300 BC'.
About 300: Magas reconquers Cyrene. 'Around 300 BC, Ptolemy dispatched Magas, then about 20 years old, to reconquer Cyrene.'

region.text: the Pentapolis, governed for Ptolemy by Magas

ledger.note: About 300: Cyrenaica passes back to Ptolemy I's Egypt under the governor Magas ('Magas subsequently served as the province's governor'; infobox governor of Cyrene 300-276; the Berenice II page: 'around 300 BCE, Ptolemy I entrusted the region to Magas'). The Cyrenaica page: 'The Pentapolis was formally annexed by Ptolemy I Soter' (undated); its infobox 'Nome (322-276 BC)'.

region.text: the Pentapolis, taken back from the Ptolemies as Magas' kingdom

ledger.note: 276: Magas makes himself king of Cyrenaica. Infobox 'King of Cyrenaica: 276-250 BC'; after Ptolemy I's death in 283 Magas 'tried to wrest independence' from Ptolemy II and crowned himself king, a date the page calls disputed ('283-280 BC and a later date in 276/274 BC'). Cliopatria starts the shape in 272.

region.text: the hinterland of Cliopatria's 272 shape beyond the Pentapolis

ledger.note: Page silent: the page names the realm Cyrenaica and gives no border; Cliopatria's 272 outline is 62,000 km2 larger than the Pentapolis, with no other state on the added land. Bridging only.

region.text: the whole kingdom, reunited with Egypt

ledger.note: 246: Cyrenaica is reunited with Egypt when Berenice II, Magas' daughter, marries Ptolemy III. 'Berenice married Ptolemy III in 246 BCE after his accession to the throne.' 'This marriage led to the re-incorporation of Cyrenaica into the Ptolemaic empire.' The Cyrenaica infobox: 'Republic (249-246 BC)', 'Nome (246-96 BC)'. Magas had died in 250 and Demetrius the Fair had been king and was killed in between (Magas page, no years). The year is the marriage's; the page dates the incorporation only through it.

region.text: Cyrene, awarded to Ptolemy VIII: the Cyrenaica cells of the Ptolemaic kingdom's 164 shape (the same cells ptolemaic-kingdom ledger 57 gives up)

ledger.note: 163: Cyrene goes to Ptolemy VIII. He "was expelled in turn in 163 BC" from Alexandria; "As a result of Roman intervention, Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene" (the page also has Ptolemy VI grant him control of Cyrenaica, and him in control of Cyrene by the end of 162 BC). Cyprus stays with his brother Ptolemy VI. The page calls him "king in Cyrene" and does not say separate kingdom; the land is a constituent of the Ptolemaic kingdom in hierarchy.csv. Mirror of ptolemaic-kingdom ledger 57 (added by review fix fx-33, 2026-11-01).

region.text: Cyrene, awarded to Ptolemy VIII: the Cyrenaica cells of the Ptolemaic kingdom's 164 shape (the same cells ptolemaic-kingdom ledger 57 gives up)

ledger.note: 145: Ptolemy VIII returns from Cyrene to be king of Egypt. "Ptolemy VI died on campaign in Syria in 145 BC"; "the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene, assume the kingship and marry his older sister, Cleopatra II"; "The Ptolemaic empire was now limited to Egypt, Cyprus, and Cyrene." Cyrene is Egyptian again. Mirror of ptolemaic-kingdom ledger 62 (added by review fix fx-33, 2026-11-01).

region.text: Cyrenaica as Ptolemy Apion's separate kingdom

ledger.note: About 105: Ptolemy Apion is given Cyrene as a separate kingdom. 'Ptolemy Apion was apparently given Cyrene as a separate kingdom ca. 105-101 BC.' The Cyrenaica page: 'It was separated from the main kingdom by Ptolemy VIII and given to his son Ptolemy Apion' (no dates); the Ptolemy VIII page: Apion 'King of Cyrenaica from an uncertain date until 96 BC'; Cliopatria's separate shape starts in 110. The earliest year of the Apion page's span is used.

region.text: the whole kingdom, bequeathed to Rome

ledger.note: 96: Ptolemy Apion dies and bequeaths Cyrenaica to Rome, which leaves it local administration until the province is organised. 'dying without heirs in 96 BC, bequeathed it to the Roman Republic' (the Ptolemy Apion page: 'Ptolemy died in 96 BC without heirs'). Both pages are silent on the years 96-78; the tributary status is roman-republic's reading (its ledger 125: 'Rome accepted it but preferred to leave administration to local rulers'), so the type is confidence 2 though the year and the land are the page's.

region.text: the whole kingdom, organised as a Roman province

ledger.note: 74: The tributary Cyrenaica ends as Rome organises the province. The infobox: 'Roman province (74 BC-643 AD)'; the text: 'by 78 BC it was organized as one administrative province together with Crete'; roman-republic (its ledger 154-155) has the quaestor sent in 74.

region.text: the whole kingdom, organised as a Roman province

ledger.note: 74: Rome annexes Cyrenaica as a province. Infobox 'Roman province (74 BC-643 AD)'; 'some confusion exists as to the exact territory Rome inherited'; the page's own text says 78 BC for the province with Crete, and this dossier follows the infobox and roman-republic's 74.
74: The last Cyrenaica, Apion's bequest, ends as a Roman province; Cliopatria draws the shape to 92, the bequest was in 96.

wars.name: Cyrenaean revolt against Ptolemy I
wars.outcome: The Cyrenaeans rebelled about 305 and Magas was sent about 300 to reconquer Cyrene; he stayed as governor to 276.
wars.note: After Ophellas's death in 308 Ptolemy had taken direct control (Ophellas governed from about 322); both revolt dates are the page's 'c.305' and 'Around 300'.

wars.name: Magas' war on Ptolemy II
wars.outcome: Magas 'was attacking Egypt from the west, as Antiochus I was attacking Palestine', married to Antiochus' daughter Apama II, but 'had to cancel his operations without results due to an internal revolt of the nomadic Libyan Marmaridae'; his later reign was 'largely peaceful'.
wars.note: The page dates neither the invasion nor the revolt; the years are Magas' kingship (276-250).

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed boundary; the coast cities are fixed, the desert edge and the Egyptian frontier are not. The western frontier with Carthage is the Altars of the Philaeni near the southern end of the Gulf of Sidra, which 'became the boundary' between Tripolitania and Cyrenaica on the Arae Philaenorum page, a legend (from Sallust) with no year there, so it stays soft.

sources.title: Magas of Cyrene
sources.note: Ophellas to 308, the revolt about 305, Magas governor 300-276 and king 276-250, the failed invasion of Egypt, the succession and Berenice's marriage. No extent of the realm. Opened twice.

sources.title: Ophellas

notes:
Repair of 2026-10-19 after the reviewer's fail verdict. Five more pages were opened (Ophellas, Berenice II, Ptolemy Apion, Ptolemy VIII Physcon, Arae Philaenorum) and the two original pages (Cyrenaica, Magas of Cyrene) were read again, seven in all against the original budget of 1-2; the extra five were opened only to date the repairs.
What changed: (1) the life is now 332-74. It begins with Alexander's tribute in 332 (the page's year; Cliopatria starts in 331, matching macedonian-empire's gain at 332 and achaemenid-empire's loss of the Libyan coast at 332) and ends with the province in 74 (the infobox; roman-republic's annexation), not at the 96 bequest. (2) The land is now Ptolemaic in 322-305 (Ophellas' army, governor to 308, then direct control), 300-276 (Magas as governor) and 246-105, and Rome's tributary in 96-74; the independent years are 332-322 (Alexander's tributary), 305-300 (the revolt), 276-246 (Magas' kingdom and its aftermath) and 105-96 (Apion). (3) The reunion with Egypt moved from 247 (Cliopatria's year) to 246 (the Berenice II marriage and the Cyrenaica infobox's Nome 246-96). (4) Apion's separate kingdom moved from 110 (Cliopatria) to 105, the earliest year of the Apion page's 'ca. 105-101'.
Cliopatria problems: (1) the first shape runs 331-292 but the land was Ptolemaic from 322 to 305 and from 300; (2) the shape of Magas' kingdom, 272-248, is 106,000 km2 against a Pentapolis of 30,700 km2, with no support for the hinterland on any page (the Magas page was read again and is silent on extent); the dates should be 276-246; (3) Cliopatria has no Cyrenaica for 291-273 and 247-111, drawing it as Ptolemaic, which the pages bear out except 105-110, when Apion's kingdom stands on the Apion page; the last shape runs to 92 although the bequest was in 96 and the province dates from 78/74.
Not settled: the extent of Magas' hinterland (confidence 1); the status of Cyrenaica in 96-74 (the pages are silent; the tributary reading is roman-republic's); the exact year of the 322 incorporation (Ophellas page and infobox 322, Berenice II page 323); Apion's kingdom years (infobox Kingdom 163-96, Apion page ca. 105-101, Cliopatria 110); the years of Demetrius the Fair and of the 249-246 republic; the Altars of the Philaeni frontier has no year.
Cross-dossier: macedonian-empire should turn the Cyrenaican part of its 332 gain from achaemenid-empire (ledger 26) into a vassal_start of cyrenaica and a vassal_end at 322; ptolemaic-kingdom should carry gains from cyrenaica at 322 and 300, losses to cyrenaica at 305 and 276, a gain at 246 and a loss at 105; roman-republic's vassal_start at 96 and vassal_end and gain at 74 now match.
No counterpart needs a new dossier: ptolemaic-kingdom and macedonian-empire exist and roman-republic exists.
